_doc: #628 Slice 2 — this app's runtime bootstrap is a real fleet LIBRARY APK, installed and updated by the Store exactly like cloud-lib-cal. Nothing here restates the artifact or the APK identity: `declared_in`+`at` point at the #618 artifact that gives the lib its content-address version, and `companion` points at the release.companions[] entry that owns the applicationId and the asset names. data/regen.sh resolves the identity, the asset names and the package from those two pointers, not from anything repeated here.
_doc_module: The ONE name. id = lib-{module}, label = cloud-lib-{module} (#474, the same rule regen.sh applies to every lib APK). Not written out twice.
_doc_kind: Changed from `artifact` to `lib` by #628 Slice 2 — that is the load-bearing edit of this whole ticket. #618/#624 published the bootstrap as a bare, uninstallable release asset (kind `artifact`, drawn only in constellation-fleet.json's `catalogue`, structurally unreachable from `apps` so no install/update path could ever be handed it). Slice 1 gave the engine a way to publish a SECOND signed APK beside this app's own; this file's `companion` pointer plus `kind: lib` is what tells data/regen.sh that APK exists and belongs in `apps`, so the Store's normal install/update path — the same one cloud-lib-cal already uses — can install and update it like every other fleet library. It has a real applicationId and a real signature now, so there is nothing structurally stopping it from being installable any more.
_doc_companion: The release.companions[] entry (build.json) that owns this lib's applicationId (com.diegonmarcos.cloudlib.rootfsnixdroid) and its published asset names (Cloud-Lib-Rootfs-Nixdroid.apk / -x86_64.apk). Read from there, not repeated here, for the same one-declaration reason `declared_in`+`at` point at the artifact instead of restating identity_files.
_doc_not_in_build_json: Still deliberately its own file and NOT a key in build.json, and that is still load-bearing: build.json is the first of the artifact's identity_files, so a fleet key added there would change the content address, rename the asset and republish the ~400 MB payload for a change that alters no byte of it. What changed with Slice 2 is only WHAT this file says the artifact is (an installable lib, not an uninstallable catalogue-only artifact) — the reason it lives apart from build.json is unchanged. The sibling ac_cloud-termux keeps the same shape so the two are read by one scan.
what: The proot + Nix store bootstrap this terminal logs into, with the agent tool belt already realized as a Nix profile generation. Installed as its own signed APK (cloud-lib-rootfs-nixdroid) beside this app, sha256-gated against the manifest baked into that APK's assets, extracted on first launch and never re-extracted while the digest matches — and never fetched over the network at all.
